evidence: ATTRIBUTION_GAP: NavierStokes/FiveRowRank.lean:311 `exists_five_row_repair` concludes `∃ dv ga, … ∧ FiveRows V G d dv ga`; NavierStokes/MeanRankUpdate.lean:194 `physical_rows_on_patch` exhibits one named solution. No declaration asserting uniqueness *of the FiveRows solution* was found; what is stated is the uniqueness one level down, at the moments: `NavierStokes.FiveProfileMoments.matrixEquiv` (NavierStokes/FiveProfileMoments.lean:207) makes the bump-moment map a linear equivalence for any injective power list, and `matrixEquiv_apply` (:221) identifies its components with the moments of `correction P c = ∑ j, c j * bump P j`.

Every clause of Lemma 8.7 is stated in Lean, each for the general object: (8.25) is `FiveRows` verbatim; solvability for arbitrary targets, the (8.17) normalization, linearity, angular independence, S_α → M_α, Δγ = γ_d, Δβ ∈ M_{α+1}, exact mass preservation and the defect cancellation each have a declaration I opened. The distribution across FiveRowRank, MeanRankUpdate, LocalRankDefect and RankStateBounds is packaging, and Lean is stronger in discharging hypothesis (8.24) for the actual base. Uniqueness of the combination is the one clause with no declaration at the five rows, but it is stated one level down as `FiveProfileMoments.matrixEquiv` over the same bumps, and the diagonal bridging it to (8.25) is proved. Hence `different_formulation` and OK, with one low-severity coverage gap.

findings.summary: The paper asserts a unique linear combination solving (8.25); no declaration stating uniqueness at the five rows was found, only existence of an explicit solution — though the uniqueness is available one level down, as `matrixEquiv`.
